option.name: --buffer
tip: Determines the number of seconds to display in the graph. (default 30)

option.name: --clear
tip: Clear the graph from the terminal after closing the program

option.name: --cmd
tip: Graph the execution time for a list of commands rather than pinging hosts

option.name: --color
tip: Assign color to a graph entry.
This option can be defined more than once as a comma separated string, and the order which the colors are provided will be matched against the hosts or commands passed to gping.

Hexadecimal RGB color codes are accepted in the form of '#RRGGBB' or the following color names: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, gray, dark-gray, light-red, light-green, light-yellow, light-blue, light-magenta, light-cyan, and white

option.name: --help
tip: Print help (see a summary with '-h')

option.name: --horizontal-margin
tip: Horizontal margin around the graph (left and right). (default 0)

option.name: --interface
tip: Interface to use when pinging.
(Linux and macOS only)

option.name: --ping-args
tip: Extra arguments to pass to `ping`.
These are platform dependent.
(Linux and macOS only)

option.name: --simple-graphics
tip: Uses dot characters instead of braille

option.name: --tcp
tip: Use TCP pings instead of ICMP

option.name: --tcp-port
tip: Port to connect to (only used for TCP pings). (default 80)

option.name: --tcp-rst
tip: How to treat a connection refused (RST) when TCP pinging. (default pong)
Possible values: pong, drop

next.name: drop
tip: Count it as a failed ping

next.name: pong
tip: Count it as a successful ping: the host answered, it just isn't listening

option.name: --version
tip: Print version

option.name: --vertical-margin
tip: Vertical margin around the graph (top and bottom). (default 1)

option.name: --watch-interval
tip: Watch interval seconds (provide partial seconds like '0.5').
Default for ping is 0.2 (1.0 on OpenBSD), default for cmd is 0.5.

option.name: --ymax
tip: Set vertical axis max (ms)

option.name: --ymin
tip: Set vertical axis min (ms)
Equivalent to --ymin=0
Resolve ping targets to IPv4 address
Resolve ping targets to IPv6 address
